subject.name: Biology
subject.description: Grade 10 Biology, Semester 1 introduces students to cell theory, cell structure, molecular biology, enzymes, cell division, stem cells, and the role of viruses in biological systems.

content.title: Disease and Cell Theory
content.description: This unit explores the relationship between cell theory and disease, focusing on infection, risk factors, and the biological causes of illness in living systems.

concepts.title: Cell Theory Disease.
concepts.description: Students learn how cell theory helps explain the biological basis of disease and how cellular function is connected to health and illness.

concepts.title: Infectious or noninfectious and factors, Vectors, Non-infectious factors
concepts.description: This concept distinguishes between infectious and non-infectious diseases and examines biological and environmental factors that influence their spread and impact.

concepts.title: Relation between diseases and economic development
concepts.description: Students analyze how disease affects communities, healthcare systems, and economic development at the local and national levels.

concepts.title: Case study: Malaria
concepts.description: This case study explores the causes, transmission, and effects of malaria to connect disease biology to public health and prevention.

content.title: Cell Structure and Types
content.description: This unit examines the basic structure of cells, compares prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, and explains how cellular organization supports function.

concepts.title: Compare and contrast eukaryotes and prokaryotes
concepts.description: Students compare the structural and functional differences between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells and relate these differences to cell organization.

concepts.title: Eukaryotic cell structure and function
concepts.description: This concept explains the major organelles of eukaryotic cells and how each structure contributes to cellular survival and function.

concepts.title: Case study: Tuberculosis
concepts.description: This case study examines tuberculosis as a disease caused by infection, highlighting symptoms, transmission, and the role of host defense.

content.title: Cell Membrane and Transport
content.description: This unit investigates the structure of the cell membrane and the mechanisms by which materials move in and out of cells through diffusion and transport systems.

concepts.title: Cell membrane (barrier function, phospholipids and proteins, fluid structure, membrane models for study of function)
concepts.description: Students study the membrane as a selective barrier and learn how phospholipids, proteins, and fluid structure support cell function.

concepts.title: Cell membrane and diffusion (diffusion, osmosis, selective permeability, protein channels and facilitated diffusion, concentration gradients, transport proteins and active transport)
concepts.description: This concept explains how molecules move across the cell membrane and how gradients and membrane proteins control transport.

concepts.title: Case study: Diabetes
concepts.description: This case study connects membrane transport and metabolic regulation to the biological causes and effects of diabetes.

content.title: DNA and RNA Structure
content.description: This unit introduces the molecular basis of heredity by examining DNA and RNA structure, nucleotide composition, and the role of genetic information.

concepts.title: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
concepts.description: Students learn the structure of DNA and how genetic information is stored, copied, and passed on during cellular processes.

concepts.title: Nucleotide subunits.
concepts.description: This concept introduces the building blocks of DNA and RNA, including sugars, phosphate groups, and nitrogenous bases.

concepts.title: Nitrogenous bases
concepts.description: Students study the chemical bases found in nucleic acids and their role in genetic coding and complementary pairing.

concepts.title: Sugar–phosphate backbone
concepts.description: This concept develops the main ideas behind Sugar–phosphate backbone and connects them to biological structure, function, and real-life applications.

concepts.title: Complementary strands
concepts.description: Students explore how complementary DNA strands bind together and why complementary base pairing is essential for replication and inheritance.

concepts.title: Double helix.
concepts.description: This concept introduces the double-helix model of DNA and explains how its shape supports storage and transmission of genetic information.

concepts.title: RNA structure
concepts.description: Students learn how RNA differs from DNA in structure and function, and how it contributes to protein synthesis.

content.title: Proteins and Enzymes
content.description: This unit explains how proteins function in cells and how enzymes regulate biological reactions through structure, activity, and environmental factors.

concepts.title: Functions of Proteins in cells (Proteins in cells, Protein classification, Enzyme structure, functions and factors affecting rates.)
concepts.description: This concept explains the many roles of proteins in cells, including structural support, catalysis, regulation, and transport.

content.title: Cell Growth and Division
content.description: This unit focuses on the cell cycle, mitotic processes, and the importance of controlled growth and division in healthy organisms.

concepts.title: Cell growth and division.
concepts.description: Students examine how cells increase in size and divide, and why regulated growth is essential for healthy tissue development.

concepts.title: Phases sequence (G1, S, G2, M)
concepts.description: This concept describes the phases of the cell cycle and the sequence of events that prepare a cell for division.

concepts.title: Normal and abnormal rates and processes
concepts.description: Students compare normal cell growth and division with abnormal patterns that may lead to disease or tumor formation.

concepts.title: Rate differentiation based on cell type
concepts.description: This concept explains why different cells divide at different rates depending on function, tissue type, and biological need.

concepts.title: Case study: Cancer
concepts.description: This case study explores how uncontrolled cell division leads to cancer and why cell-cycle regulation is essential to health.

content.title: Stem Cells
content.description: This unit explores stem cell types, differentiation, embryonic development, and the medical potential and ethical issues surrounding stem cell therapy.

concepts.title: STEM cells types according to differentiation (Totipotent, Pluripotent, Multipoint)
concepts.description: Students learn how stem cells vary in differentiation potential and how this affects their role in development and repair.

concepts.title: Types of STEM cells according to its presence (Embryonic, Adults (somatic))
concepts.description: This concept distinguishes stem cells based on their origin and explains the differences between embryonic and adult stem cells.

concepts.title: Layers of embryo (Ectoderm, Endoderm, Mesoderm)
concepts.description: Students examine the primary germ layers and their roles in forming specialized tissues and organs in an embryo.

concepts.title: STEM cells as a treatment (Treatment for leukemia, Umbilical cord blood STEM cells therapy, Bone marrow transplant)
concepts.description: This concept explores the medical use of stem cells in treating diseases such as leukemia and the importance of tissue matching and transplantation.

concepts.title: New researches treatment for diabetes
concepts.description: Students evaluate how stem cell research is contributing to new treatments for diabetes and other chronic diseases.

concepts.title: The STEM cells debate.
concepts.description: This concept examines the scientific promise and ethical questions surrounding stem cell research and therapy.

content.title: Viral Interactions
content.description: This unit examines how viruses interact with cells, reproduce, and affect host biological systems, including diseases such as HIV.

concepts.title: The relationship between cell protein and viral protein
concepts.description: Students analyze how viruses use host cell machinery and exploit protein interactions to reproduce and spread infection.

concepts.title: Receptor proteins and enzymes
concepts.description: This concept explains how receptor proteins and enzymes contribute to viral entry, host recognition, and the regulation of infection.

concepts.title: Protein manufacture of virus utilizing cell organelles.
concepts.description: Students study how viruses hijack cellular organelles to produce viral proteins and replicate their genetic material.

concepts.title: HIV virus mechanism of infection and replication.
concepts.description: This concept describes the HIV life cycle, how the virus infects host cells, and how it uses cellular machinery to replicate.

concepts.title: Case study: HIV (disease symptoms)
concepts.description: This case study explores HIV infection, progression, and symptoms, linking viral biology to disease outcomes and treatment.

content.title: Question Bank
content.description: This section contains practice questions and exam-style activities designed to reinforce biological concepts and assess understanding.

content.title: Revision
content.description: This section summarizes the key biological ideas and exam skills needed for review before tests and final assessments.

content.title: References
content.description: This section gathers helpful reference books and supporting resources for additional learning and self-study.
